disclaimer: This report is for educational and wellness purposes only. It is not a medical diagnosis and does not replace advice from a qualified healthcare professional. HbA1c results should be confirmed by your doctor. Do not start, stop or change any medication without medical advice.

status.label: In the prediabetes range
status.explanation: Your HbA1c is between 5.7% and 6.4%, the range used for prediabetes. This is a common and often reversible stage where lifestyle changes make the biggest difference.

summary: Your HbA1c of 5.7 falls in the prediabetes range, which means your blood sugar is a bit higher than ideal but still has room to improve with lifestyle changes. Key risk factors for you include being overweight, regular alcohol use, being over 45, and existing high cholesterol or triglycerides. The most valuable next steps are getting your lipid profile and HbA1c checked regularly, staying active most days, and following your food plan's limits on saturated fat and focus on fibre. Small, steady changes now can make a meaningful difference to your long-term health.

risk_factors.label: Body weight above the healthy range
Existing health condition: High cholesterol or triglycerides

comorbidity_assessment.note: Elevated cholesterol or triglycerides often occur alongside higher blood sugar, and both can affect your heart and blood vessel health over time. Managing your diet and activity can support healthier levels of both.

constraints: Keep saturated fat low (limit ghee, butter, coconut oil, red and processed meat); avoid trans fats (vanaspati, many fried and bakery foods).
Include soluble fibre daily (oats, barley, pulses, psyllium) and unsaturated fats (nuts, seeds, olive or mustard oil in small amounts).

foods_to_eat: Oats and barley for soluble fibre
Fatty fish like salmon or sardines
Nuts and seeds such as walnuts and flaxseed
Olive oil and mustard oil in small amounts
Whole grains like quinoa and brown rice
foods_to_avoid: Red and processed meats like bacon, sausage, and salami
Butter, ghee, and coconut oil in large amounts
Fried and bakery items made with trans fats (vanaspati)
White bread, white rice, and other refined grains
Sweets, pastries, and desserts high in added sugar
Full-fat dairy products like cream and regular cheese
plan.portion_guidance: Aim to fill half your plate with non-starchy vegetables, one quarter with lean protein like fish, poultry, or legumes, and one quarter with whole grains such as quinoa, brown rice, or barley. Use measuring cups or your hand as a guide: a fist-sized portion of grains, a palm-sized portion of protein, and a cupped handful of nuts or seeds.
plan.hydration: Drink water throughout the day, aiming for about 8 cups (64 oz). Herbal tea and plain sparkling water are good options. Limit alcohol intake, as it can affect blood sugar and triglyceride levels, and avoid sugary drinks and juices.
based_on: high cholesterol or triglycerides: low saturated fat, soluble fibre focus

exercise: Start with brisk walking or cycling for 20-30 minutes, 4-5 days a week, gradually building toward at least 150 minutes of moderate aerobic activity weekly, since aerobic activity helps improve HDL cholesterol and triglyceride levels.
Add simple muscle-strengthening exercises, such as bodyweight squats, resistance bands, or light weights, on 2 non-consecutive days a week.
Increase intensity or duration gradually as your fitness improves, listening to your body and resting when needed.
lifestyle.walking_goal: Begin with 15-20 minutes of walking daily this week, then build up to at least 30 minutes a day, 5 days a week, over the coming month.
lifestyle.weight_management: Since your BMI falls in the overweight category, aim for gradual, sustainable weight loss through a balanced eating pattern and regular physical activity. Even a modest reduction in weight can help improve cholesterol levels and blood sugar control over time.
lifestyle.sleep: Aim for 7-9 hours of sleep each night. Try to keep a consistent sleep and wake time, limit screens before bed, and keep your bedroom cool, dark, and quiet to support restful sleep.
stress: Practice slow, deep breathing exercises for 5-10 minutes daily to help calm your nervous system.
Try mindfulness or meditation apps, or simply take short breaks during the day to stretch and reset.
Consider regular physical activity and time outdoors, both of which can help reduce stress levels.
behaviour_change: Since you drink regularly, consider cutting back on alcohol intake, as reducing alcohol can help improve cholesterol levels, support weight management, and improve blood sugar control. Try setting limits, having alcohol-free days, or swapping to non-alcoholic alternatives.
Build small, consistent habits such as taking a daily walk, choosing water over sugary drinks, or adding vegetables to meals, since small sustainable changes often lead to lasting results.
Track your progress with a journal or app to notice patterns and celebrate small wins along the way.

monitoring.name: Lipid profile (cholesterol)
monitoring.why: Diabetes and high cholesterol together raise the risk of heart disease and stroke.
monitoring.frequency: Every year (at least every 5 years if you are under 40), or as your doctor advises
risk_indicators: Existing cholesterol problem or heart disease

monitoring.name: HbA1c
monitoring.why: Catches progression from prediabetes to diabetes early.

monitoring.name: Fasting blood sugar
monitoring.why: Shows your blood glucose after an overnight fast and complements HbA1c.
monitoring.frequency: Alongside your HbA1c test, or as your doctor advises

monitoring.name: Blood pressure
monitoring.why: High blood pressure multiplies the heart and kidney risks of high blood glucose.
monitoring.frequency: At every doctor visit; at home regularly if you have high blood pressure

preventive_actions: Schedule a lipid profile test soon since it's highlighted as a priority for you.
Aim for regular aerobic activity most days to help both blood sugar and cholesterol levels.
Limit saturated fat sources like ghee, butter, and processed meat, and avoid trans fats from fried or bakery foods.
Add soluble fibre foods such as oats, barley, and pulses to your daily meals.
Consider reducing alcohol intake, since regular use can affect blood sugar and liver health.
Keep track of your calorie target of 1850 to support gradual, healthy weight management.
